subject: Post-call recap — MedSync dedicated GPU qualification and isolation needs
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@medsync.ai>, Tom Waller <tom@medsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — MedSync dedicated GPU qualification and isolation needs

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. High-level notes below — please correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you described:
- Production latency spikes during nightly batch ingestion and inference on PHI data (current infra shared with other workloads).
- Cost unpredictability from on-demand cloud GPUs during peak training/processing runs.
- Compliance requirement to ensure logical separation of PHI inference workloads for auditors.

Goals you shared:
- Dedicated, isolated serving pool for clinical inference workloads (start-of-life target: Q4 production).
- P95 latency target for inference < 300 ms for typical 1k–2k token request mix.
- Predictable monthly unit cost with a committed baseline and well-understood burst policy.

Initial sizing / isolation summary (our suggestion to qualify):
- Committed pool: ~6x H100-equivalent GPUs (sized for your current 200 rps baseline, with 2x headroom for growth).
- Burst: ability to overflow to Redwood hosted capacity for short spikes up to additional 50% throughput.
- Isolation: tenant-silo with dedicated VPC endpoints and KMS integration for keys — acceptable for your PHI requirements per our security brief.

SLA / operational targets discussed:
- Target uptime: 99.95% for reserved pool (we can discuss uplift to 99.99% for enterprise SLA).
- Latency: ops playbook to maintain p95 <= 300 ms; deeper tuning after technical dive.
- Auditability: request / response logs (obfuscated) + per-request trace IDs available.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Diego: send capacity template + privacy brief (attached) — ACTION: you to confirm baseline throughput and peak windows — ETA: today.
2) MedSync: confirm procurement contact (you mentioned Sofia) and preferred billing cadence — ACTION: Elena/Tom to confirm — ETA: 2 business days.
3) Redwood: schedule technical deep-dive with SEs to validate pool sizing and isolation knobs (Marissa will lead) — ACTION: propose slots — ETA: by EOD tomorrow.
4) Docs: we’ll share an initial commercial construct (committed pool + burst policy) and a rough cost estimate after the SE call.

Attachments: medsync_capacity_template.xlsx, redwood_privacy_brief.pdf

Appreciate the candor on constraints — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the SE deep-dive.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: (415) 555-0198 | diego.fernandez@redwood.com

---

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@medsync.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Waller <tom@medsync.ai>, Sofia Delgado <sofia@medsync.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — MedSync dedicated GPU qualification and isolation needs

Diego — thanks for the concise recap. This looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline we want to commit to initially is closer to 4x H100-equivalent (we ran the numbers overnight) with clear ability to burst to 8x for scheduled jobs. Is that something that maps cleanly to Redwood’s reserved capacity constructs?
- For compliance: auditors will want separate network controls and evidence of tenant isolation. Can you confirm the artifacts you can share (SOC 2 section, VPC topology sketch, KMS flow)?
- Procurement: confirmed — Sofia Delgado (sofia@medsync.ai) will own PO. She asked if we can get an initial term-sheet or a rough SOW before the deep-dive so finance has something to review.

Also looping in Tom for volume/throughput nuance — Tom, we have two heavy nightly windows: 0200–0400 PST and another at 1200–1300 PST. Those are the spikes we’re most worried about.

Thanks — Elena
CTO, MedSync.ai

Appreciate the clarifications, Elena. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a committed 4x H100-equivalent pool with burst to hosted capacity up to 2x nominal (effectively sizing to 8x during bursts), and we can provide the compliance artifacts you need. More detail below.

Sizing & burst model:
- Committed: 4x H100-equivalent reserved pool (baseline). We will size job concurrency and throughput for your two nightly windows during SE deep-dive.
- Burst policy: automatic overflow to Redwood hosted capacity for transient spikes (configurable threshold and max burst cap). Burst is metered separately; we’ll provide estimates in the commercial construct.

Compliance artifacts we can share (preliminary):
- SOC 2 summary and audit point mapping (PDF)
- VPC/topology diagram and example network ACL config (redacted)
- KMS/HSM integrations and key lifecycle overview
- Sample audit log extract format (fields and retention)
We’ll attach the privacy brief and a pointer to our security playbook in the follow-up email.

Commercial/PO path:
- We can prepare a short term-sheet (non-binding) that outlines committed pool size, burst policy, basic SLA, and estimated monthly costs. We’ll include an example billing cadence (monthly/quarterly). I’ll push a draft to Sofia and CC you.
- If you want an expedited path, we can issue a preliminary DocuSign for PO approval tied to the committed baseline; this is optional until after SE validation.

Proposed next meeting: SE deep-dive — Marissa will propose 2x 60-min slots tomorrow. Please indicate which works for you.

Attachment(s): redwood_capacity_playbook.pdf

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com
